section: Atmospheric Disturbances – Tropical Cyclones, Temperate Cyclones, Anticyclones, Thunderstorms, Tornadoes
sub: Tropical Cyclones – Formation and Where They Form
text: None in the South Atlantic and SE Pacific – UPSC 2015 key: ITCZ seldom occurs there; also cold currents (Benguela, Humboldt) keep SST low.

section: Elements and Factors of Climate; World Climatic Classification (koeppen)
sub: Mediterranean Climate and Hot Deserts
text: Hot deserts 15–30°, on western margins; most likely near 23° (Tropics): subtropical high pressure + offshore trade winds + cold currents. Sahara, Kalahari, Namib, Atacama, Arabian, Thar, Great Australian.

section: Ocean-atmosphere Interaction – El Nino, La Nina, Enso, Iod, Walker Circulation
sub: El Nino – Meaning, Mechanism and Effects
text: El Nino = an abnormally warm ocean current that appears off the coast of Peru and Ecuador in the eastern (and central) tropical Pacific and flows south along the west coast of South America, replacing the cold Peruvian (Humboldt) current. It is an ocean event, not an air mass, a wind or a low-pressure centre (CDS 2011).

section: Ocean-atmosphere Interaction – El Nino, La Nina, Enso, Iod, Walker Circulation
sub: El Nino – Meaning, Mechanism and Effects
text: The El Nino current carries warmer, less saline water (the warm, rain-freshened pool of the western Pacific spreads east) – NDA 2010 "all four" statements.

section: Ocean-atmosphere Interaction – El Nino, La Nina, Enso, Iod, Walker Circulation
sub: El Nino – Meaning, Mechanism and Effects
text: APPSC: Peru warm current + "Christ child" + 2014 Indian rainfall deficit = all three correct.

section: Ocean Movements – Waves, Tides and Ocean Currents of the World
sub: Ocean Currents of the World – Warm and Cold
text: Warm currents flow from the equator towards the poles, usually on the east coasts of continents in low and middle latitudes; cold currents flow towards the equator, usually on the west coasts (NCERT).

section: Ocean Movements – Waves, Tides and Ocean Currents of the World
sub: Ocean Currents of the World – Warm and Cold
text: Odd ones: Humboldt is NOT warm (APPSC); Agulhas is NOT cold; Kuroshio is NOT cold; Canary is NOT warm and not in the Pacific; Benguela does not flow in the North Atlantic; Peruvian is the only Pacific current among Benguela, Brazil, South Equatorial.

section: Ocean Movements – Waves, Tides and Ocean Currents of the World
sub: Ocean Currents of the World – Warm and Cold
text: Pairs of warm currents: North Atlantic Drift and Brazil; all cold: Humboldt and Benguela; Canaries and Benguela.

section: Ocean Movements – Waves, Tides and Ocean Currents of the World
sub: Tides
text: Tidal currents: tidal water channelled between islands or into bays and estuaries forms tidal currents.

section: Ocean Movements – Waves, Tides and Ocean Currents of the World
sub: Effects of Currents – Fishing Grounds, Climate and Upwelling
text: Best fishing grounds form where warm and cold ocean currents meet (mixing brings nutrients and plankton), mainly between 40° and 60° – asked 4 times (APPSC 2002 twice, UPSC 2013 twice).

section: Ocean Movements – Waves, Tides and Ocean Currents of the World
sub: Effects of Currents – Fishing Grounds, Climate and Upwelling
text: The Labrador Current meets the Gulf Stream at the Grand Banks, not near Vancouver Island (NDA 2010: I and II only).

section: Ocean Movements – Waves, Tides and Ocean Currents of the World
sub: Effects of Currents – Fishing Grounds, Climate and Upwelling
text: Cold currents on west coasts help form arid climates; warm currents warm the coasts beside them; currents keep Earth's heat balance.

section: Ocean Movements – Waves, Tides and Ocean Currents of the World
sub: Causes of Ocean Currents
text: Ocean currents = large masses of surface water circulating in regular patterns; the slow surface movement of water, set in motion mainly by prevailing winds, help keep the heat balance, are affected by the configuration of the ocean – UPSC 2002: all four statements correct.

section: Ocean Movements – Waves, Tides and Ocean Currents of the World
sub: Causes of Ocean Currents
text: Equatorial Counter Current flows west to east between the North and South Equatorial Currents (through the doldrums) because their convergence piles up water in the west (UPSC 2015, asked twice).

section: Ocean Movements – Waves, Tides and Ocean Currents of the World
sub: Causes of Ocean Currents
text: Surface currents = upper 400 m, about 10% of ocean water; deep currents = 90%.

section: Ocean Movements – Waves, Tides and Ocean Currents of the World
sub: Causes of Ocean Currents
text: Waves = oscillations moving energy; tides = periodic vertical rise and fall; currents = continuous horizontal flow with major effects on climate, fisheries and navigation; currents redistribute heat, so they influence climate.

section: Ocean Movements – Waves, Tides and Ocean Currents of the World
sub: Gyres and the Sargasso Sea
text: Sargasso Sea (North Atlantic): the only sea with no coastline – bounded by currents: Gulf Stream (W), North Atlantic Drift (N), Canary (E), North Equatorial (S); calm, warm, salty; named after its floating Sargassum weed (typical marine vegetation).
